figures.caption: Figure 4: Per-sample failure analysis (RefCOCO val). Left: default vs. best-query IoU per sample—failures (red) lie above the diagonal. Right: distribution of the gap among failure cases (mean: 45.9%).
Figure 3: The failure-case bottleneck. 7–18% of samples (red) account for 40–68% of the total error budget. 27–52% is recoverable via best-query selection.

Figure 16: Top-12 failure cases on RefCOCO val. Each cell: default query (left, red overlay) vs. best query (right, green overlay). Ground-truth contour in yellow; IoU gap at top. A correct mask exists among the candidates but is not selected by the default heuristic.

Table 4: Comparison with re-ranking baselines (average mIoU change across all 8 evaluation splits). Heuristic strategies that ignore inter-query comparison either degrade or match the default. Venice-H1 is the only method to achieve consistent positive improvement without regression on any split.
Figure 6: Per-split improvement breakdown. Venice-H1 achieves positive ∆ on all splits where the best-query gap is non-trivial.

Table 3: Comparison with state-of-the-art methods on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg (mIoU). † cIoU metric. Venice-H1 operates as a post-hoc re-ranker on the frozen DeRIS-L output, adding ∼11 M parameters and <1 ms latency. Bold/underline denote best/second-best within our evaluation pipeline (bottom block) only. Published DeRIS-L numbers (grey) are shown for reference and are not ranked.§
Table 5: Ablation study on RefCOCO val (evaluated in our pipeline, baseline Q0 = 85.46% mIoU). ∆full/∆fail: mIoU change on all / failure-only samples.
Figure 7: IoU distribution of default (Q0) vs. best-query selections across evaluation splits.
